strokeOrderSource.variation: The cited freehand lesson demonstrates isolated ش body-first: one continuous right-to-left Naskh movement shapes three teeth and flows directly into the final bowl. The writer then lifts for three separate dots above in lower-left, lower-right, then centered-upper order. Contextual joins shorten the final bowl before following letters; this four-stroke Persian learner path fits the vendored Noto Naskh outline and preserves Persian-scoped provenance rather than borrowing the independently verified Arabic or Urdu ش sources.
